title: TxQueue.complete() removes by value-equality instead of entry identity
description: tx_queue.py:523: self._entries.remove(entry) deletes the first value-equal TxQueueEntry (plain @dataclass __eq__), not necessarily the reserved object. fail() (567) and cancel_reservation() (579) already use identity; complete() is the one inconsistent site. Unreachable today (complete is only called on the reserved head while the queue cannot mutate under _tx_lock), but a byte-identical entry pushed to the head while a twin is in flight (lock-bypassing push, same-ms enqueue_time_ms) would remove the wrong object and leave the stale twin eligible to re-reserve -> duplicate transmission. Fix: identity scan (e.g. next(i for i,e in enumerate(self._entries) if e is entry)) mirroring fail()/cancel_reservation(). Related: project-LICHEN-worker6-gwpt. Found by correctness codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-9qpz.
